ordered_diagnoses: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries

s1.syndrome_frame: Abnormal cardiac conduction and morphology with unusual cardiac positioning
salient_findings: Apex of the heart located at the right side of the chest
Hepatic dullness in the left subcostal region
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 80s
No previous medical records available
Patient denied any history of chest pain
ECG showed wide complex rhythm at rate of 76 beats/min
Right bundle branch block morphology on ECG
QRS duration of 120 milliseconds
Negative P waves with pathological Q waves in leads I and aVL
Positive P waves in lead V1
Biphasic P waves in leads V2 through V6
Pathological Q waves in leads V5 and V6
Transthoracic Echocardiogram showed right atrium and right ventricle on the left side
Left atrium and left ventricle on the right side with its apex directed to the right

shortlist.label: Dextrocardia with situs solitus
shortlist.why_kept: ECG and echocardiogram findings consistent with dextrocardia, and patient's age suggests a congenital condition

shortlist.label: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
shortlist.why_kept: Echocardiogram showed right atrium and ventricle on the left, and left atrium and ventricle on the right, consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Cardiac malposition
shortlist.why_kept: Physical examination and echocardiogram findings indicate abnormal cardiac positioning

shortlist.label: Heterotaxy syndrome

shortlist.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, this condition is still plausible given the patient's ECG and echocardiogram findings

raw.rationale: The patient's heart apex is located on the right side of the chest, and the transthoracic echocardiogram shows the right atrium and ventricle on the left side, with the left atrium and ventricle on the right side, which is consistent with dextrocardia. The presence of situs solitus is suggested by the location of the liver (hepatic dullness) in the left subcostal region, indicating normal abdominal organ positioning.

rejected.label: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
rejected.why: This condition would typically involve abnormal great vessel relationships, which are not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Cardiac malposition
rejected.why: This term is too broad and does not specifically account for the combination of dextrocardia and normal abdominal organ positioning found in this patient.

rejected.label: Heterotaxy syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves abnormal arrangement of abdominal organs, which is not indicated by the location of hepatic dullness in the left subcostal region.

rejected.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
rejected.why: Situs inversus would involve reversal of abdominal organ positioning, which is not consistent with the liver's location in the left subcostal region.
